title: Decompose 19 oversize Python files to an empty allowlist: one sub-package per file via the canonical barrel pattern, file-disjoint slices, with pipelines.py (_run_pipeline) and gateway.py as multi-PR sub-programs
summary: Pure-refactor decomposition of all 19 allowlisted files into sub-packages following docs/guides/decomposition-pattern.md and the scripts/select_tests/ reference. Every file foo.py -> foo/ with __init__.py as the explicit per-symbol re-export barrel (stable public API) and underscore-prefixed private submodules; routes keep @bp.route/@app.route decorators in __init__.py delegating to submodule bodies (decision-8); class-dominated files keep the class identity in __init__.py with method bodies extracted to module-level helpers taking explicit self (method-modules-on-class). Each landing: step-0 git mv baseline commit, then cluster commits, allowlist entry dropped, CLAUDE.md seam table row added/retagged, make lint + make test-all green. The two structural outliers are addressed head-on, not deferred: gateway/gateway.py (10,385 lines, 46 @app.route) decomposes into ~10 route/helper submodules with three over-cap clusters (git, gh, jira) each further-split in-slice; orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py (27,211 lines, 16 routes) is a multi-PR sub-program whose hardest piece, the _run_pipeline phase-transition state machine (~3,042 lines), splits into a thin orchestration loop (__init__ of a _run_loop/ sub-sub-package) plus per-phase handlers + an extracted consensus-cycle and HITL-gate. All 19 slices are file-disjoint at the source level; cross-slice contention is mechanical and resolved by the section-(e) rebase recipe, but it spans FIVE shared write targets, not three: scripts/file-size-allowlist.yaml, the CLAUDE.md seam tables, AND orchestrator/Dockerfile + gateway/Dockerfile. Eight decompositions also require a Dockerfile COPY edit because converting a top-level module that ships via a NON-recursive `*.py` COPY glob (orchestrator/{state_store,peer_consensus,mcp_tools,kubernetes_spawner,gateway_client}; gateway/{gateway,worktree_manager,git_client}) to a sub-package dir means the new dir is no longer copied -> ModuleNotFoundError in the running image, while make lint/make test-all stay GREEN against the source tree. sandbox/entrypoint.py additionally needs a thin executable shim (it ships via a single-file COPY and is invoked directly). This Dockerfile work is in-slice and is a precondition of the pure-refactor invariant (a broken image is a behavior change). Independent per-file slices still land value even if the two outliers stall (the failure mode of #2817/#3111). Scope is LOCKED by operator directive: all 19 files, empty allowlist, no descope.

problem_statement.description: make lint caps Python source at 1,500 lines / 100KB (#2250, motivated by the Read tool's ~25k-token soft limit; #2248). Nineteen files are grandfathered in scripts/file-size-allowlist.yaml and grow unbounded while the lint ratchets everything else. This program drives those baselines to zero so agent navigation cost is paid once, not per BRC cycle. The pattern + worked reference landed in PR #2335 (merged); no decomposition slice has ever landed (refresh of #3111 -> #2817 -> #2261). Acceptance = empty files: map + make lint/make test-all green at every landing boundary, pure refactor, no behavior change.

pattern_recap.source: docs/guides/decomposition-pattern.md (canonical) + scripts/select_tests/ (worked reference) + PR #2335 (merged template; coder reads its diff first).
rules: (a) Sub-package, not sibling files: foo.py -> foo/__init__.py; clusters are private _<cluster>.py siblings (decision-1, -6).
(b) Step-0 baseline: git mv foo.py foo/__init__.py as its own bisectable commit, make test-all green, THEN carve clusters. Keeps git blame/bisect clean.
(c) Explicit per-symbol re-exports in __init__.py (decision-5); no wildcard re-exports. The barrel is the stable public API (decision-7).

(d) External-importer audit per cluster (git grep recipe section d) before extracting; re-export every externally-referenced symbol. Skip a re-export only for symbols that are BOTH underscore-prefixed AND referenced solely inside the file's own package.

(e) Method-modules-on-class for class-dominated files: keep the class object in __init__.py; extract method bodies to module-level functions in _<cluster>.py taking explicit self; methods become thin delegating wrappers. Preserves patch('module.ClassName') and the class as public surface.

(f) Routes convention (decision-8): @bp.route / @app.route decorators STAY in __init__.py on thin wrappers; submodule functions hold the bodies. Uniform for orchestrator Blueprints and the gateway @app.route surface.
(g) Dual-import shape stays consistent within a sub-package (all dual try/except OR all relative; never mixed).
(h) Further-split in-slice (section g): a submodule landing at/over cap is split again within the same slice (recursive barrels compose) -- never a fresh allowlist entry.
(i) Allowlist drop per landing (section e); CLAUDE.md seam table updated per landing; bugs surfaced -> separate follow-up issue (section h), never bundled. Branches prefixed egg/.

run_pipeline_state_machine.constraint: Issue non-negotiable #7: _run_pipeline (~3,042 lines, lines ~23345-26386) MUST be decomposed directly, not deferred. Mechanical extraction won't work; the pattern doc's prior design is a thin orchestration loop + per-phase handlers.
run_pipeline_state_machine.structure_observed: A setup preamble (load pipeline, capture run-epoch, create worktrees, sync with divergence reconcile, init health monitor) -> a `while True` phase loop. Each iteration: phase-start (mark RUNNING, emit event, conditional context-PR at implement entry) -> overseer spawn (gated by _overseer_should_be_present) -> sandbox env build -> an inner review cycle (`while True`: reset tester gaps, capture cycle HEAD, slice-DAG decision/auto-populate, run via _run_implement_phase_slices OR _run_concurrent_phase, failure handling on non-zero exit, success path: mark COMPLETE, commit/sync statefiles, populate-contract-from-plan on plan, sync HITL decisions, write BRC history, unresolved-gap gate on implement, HITL phase-gate with revise/approve branches that can `continue` the inner loop) -> phase advance (auto-advance context PR, overseer teardown, compute next phases via _next_phases_for_epic, write apply handoff / drain wontdo, update current_phase + run_epoch, clear concurrent state, respawn driver thread, return) -> exception handlers (PipelineNotFoundError spurious-transient retry/respawn; general exception -> lock + mark FAILED + push backup) -> finally (teardown health monitor, clean worktree unless superseded by epoch bump).

Each composes phase-start, overseer spawn, the consensus cycle, the success/finalize path, and advance. Shared scaffolding stays in helpers to avoid four near-duplicate bodies; the phase-specific deltas (plan populates contract; apply drains wontdo; implement does slice-DAG routing + gap gate) live in the respective handler. submodules.name: _hitl_gate.py
submodules.role: The HITL phase-gate block extracted: idempotent check-for-pending-or-queue, await resolution, JSON-first/legacy-bare parse, request-changes follow-up prompt, revise branch (snapshot BRC tracker, clear concurrent state, stale-container teardown -> signal the cycle to re-run) vs approve branch (queue contract-decisions bridge, restore COMPLETE, persist gate resolution, commit/push). Returns (approved: bool, revision_feedback: str|None).

submodules.name: _advance.py
submodules.role: Phase-advance extracted: auto-advance context PR, overseer teardown, compute next phases, apply-handoff / wontdo-drain, update current_phase + run_epoch, clear concurrent state, respawn driver thread for the next phase. Returns the next phase or None (pipeline complete).

invariants_to_preserve: No behavior change: the phase-transition semantics, epoch-bump supersession, spurious-PNFE retry, and the finally-block worktree cleanup gating MUST be byte-equivalent in effect.
The inner review-cycle `continue` on HITL revise must still re-run the phase without advancing -- the extracted _hitl_gate signals the cycle rather than driving the loop itself.

Driver-thread respawn (_spawn_pipeline_run_thread) on advance is the mechanism that hands the next phase to a fresh thread; keep it in _advance.py and ensure the loop returns after respawn (does not fall through).
Health-monitor teardown + worktree cleanup happen in the loop's finally, NOT in a handler, so a handler early-return cannot leak them.
run_pipeline_state_machine.test_strategy: Per non-negotiable #10 (guidance): the existing scenario-organized _run_pipeline tests keep patching through routes.pipelines.* (the barrel re-exports the handlers + the loop), so they do not move. Extracting handlers as module-level functions makes the state machine unit-testable per phase for the first time, but adding such tests is a FOLLOW-UP (section h), not part of the pure-refactor slice.

slice_dag_guidance.ownership: task_planner owns the final slice DAG / ordering / PR packaging. This artifact provides the binding structural facts: per-file submodule cut-lines, the two outliers' multi-PR shape, and the contention model.
slice_dag_guidance.file_disjointness: All 19 decompositions are file-disjoint at the SOURCE level -- each touches its own foo.py -> foo/ tree and nothing else's source. They are therefore parallelizable.
slice_dag_guidance.shared_contention: FIVE shared write targets create MECHANICAL (not logical) conflicts across slices: (1) scripts/file-size-allowlist.yaml -- every slice deletes its own entry; (2) the CLAUDE.md seam tables (orchestrator/, gateway/, sandbox/, shared/) -- every slice ADDS its own row; (3) orchestrator/Dockerfile -- the 5 top-level orchestrator slices (state_store, peer_consensus, mcp_tools, kubernetes_spawner, gateway_client) each add an explicit `COPY orchestrator/<name>/ ./<name>/` line; (4) gateway/Dockerfile -- the 3 gateway slices (gateway, worktree_manager, git_client) each add `COPY gateway/<name>/ ./<name>/`; (5) sandbox/Dockerfile -- the entrypoint.py slice adjusts its single-file COPY (or adds a shim). All are additive/independent edits that conflict on the same file; resolve via the section-(e) rebase recipe (take theirs for other slices' edits, re-apply your own). They do NOT justify serializing the program.
slice_dag_guidance.dockerfile_packaging: BINDING structural fact (risk_analyst R3, verified against the live tree). orchestrator/Dockerfile:44 ships top-level modules via `COPY orchestrator/*.py ./` -- a NON-recursive glob (proven: routes/ and health_checks/ have their OWN explicit `COPY orchestrator/<dir>/` lines at 45-46 precisely because the glob does not recurse). gateway/Dockerfile:67 is identical (`COPY gateway/*.py ./`). Converting any of those top-level modules to a sub-package dir means the dir is NOT copied -> ModuleNotFoundError at container start, while make lint + make test-all (which run against the SOURCE TREE, not a built image) stay GREEN. So each affected slice MUST, in the SAME slice, add the explicit `COPY orchestrator/<name>/ ./<name>/` (or gateway equivalent) line and verify with an image build or in-container import. AFFECTED (8): orchestrator/{state_store, peer_consensus, mcp_tools, kubernetes_spawner, gateway_client}, gateway/{gateway, worktree_manager, git_client}. SPECIAL -- sandbox/entrypoint.py: ships via single-file `COPY sandbox/entrypoint.py /usr/local/bin/entrypoint.py` (sandbox/Dockerfile:386) and is invoked as that exact path (ENTRYPOINT at :391). Package conversion breaks both -> keep a thin executable entrypoint.py shim that imports the new entrypoint/ sub-package, OR change the COPY + ENTRYPOINT together. UNVERIFIED (confirm before landing): sandbox/egg_lib/{orch_cli,contract_cli} have NO egg_lib COPY in sandbox/Dockerfile (ship via docker-setup.py / prepare-sandbox-build-context.py / pip + the whole-repo `COPY . /opt/egg-runtime/` at :361) -- likely SAFE via setuptools find_packages but confirm the package dir is importable in-container. orchestrator/overseer/monitor.py: overseer/ has NO explicit COPY line today and is runtime-imported via `from overseer.* import` in pipelines.py -- a possible PRE-EXISTING latent shipping gap; the monitor/ slice MUST verify the sub-package ships (and may need to add `COPY orchestrator/overseer/`) before it lands. SAFE (no Dockerfile work, ship under a recursive dir COPY): the routes/ files (pipelines, signals, deployment, phases, decisions, event_prompt) under `COPY orchestrator/routes/`; plan_parser under `COPY shared/egg_contracts/`.
slice_dag_guidance.ordering_heuristic: Per the issue's explicit recommendation (and the #2817/#3111 failure history): FRONT-LOAD the independent smaller per-file slices so they land value even if the two outliers stall again. Suggested priority waves (NOT hard dependencies -- all slices may run in parallel up to EGG_ORCH_MAX_PARALLEL_SLICES): Wave 1 (clean, ~1-1.3x cap, fast wins + a second CLI worked example): contract_cli, decisions, state_store, phases, deployment, event_prompt, plan_parser. Wave 2 (~2-2.5x, mostly single sub-sub-split): monitor, entrypoint, peer_consensus, git_client, worktree_manager. Wave 3 (~2.9-3.4x, one over-cap cluster each): mcp_tools, kubernetes_spawner, signals. Wave 4 (large, multiple over-cap clusters): gateway_client, orch_cli. Wave 5 (outliers, each a STACK of PRs): gateway.py, then pipelines.py (with _run_loop/ extracted LAST).
slice_dag_guidance.no_hard_deps: Recommended dependencies between slices: NONE (file-disjoint). The waves are a scheduling/priority hint, not a DAG edge. The planner may parallelize freely; the only reason to stagger is to bound mechanical allowlist/CLAUDE.md rebase churn.
